summary.headline: Stanley Lifestyles Q2 FY27 revenue rose to Rs 10,706 lakh (flat YoY vs 10,542 lakh) and EBITDA to Rs 1,989 lakh at 18.6% margin.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 10,706 lakh, up 7.8% QoQ from Rs 9,935 lakh in Q1 and roughly flat against Rs 10,542 lakh a year earlier. H1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 20,641 lakh from Rs 21,409 lakh. EBITDA was Rs 1,989 lakh (18.6% margin), up 15.5% QoQ from Rs 1,722 lakh, with a rupee depreciation hit to gross margin. Management said delayed residential handovers are pushing back furniture purchases by premium-housing buyers, and it is proceeding with amalgamating subsidiaries into Stanley Lifestyles Ltd.

financial_highlights.change: +7.8% QoQ from Rs 9,935 lakh; vs Rs 10,542 lakh in Q2 FY26 (about +1.6% YoY)
vs Rs 21,409 lakh in H1 FY26 (about -3.6% YoY)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 17.19 crore (as referenced in call; Q1 figure cited as Rs 14.29 crore)
financial_highlights.change: Increase attributed to increments, reversal of NPD capitalisation, and senior management hiring

financial_highlights.value: About Rs 170 crore (per management in Q&A)
financial_highlights.change: Management said cash remains strong after large-format store investments

segments.name: Retail (company-operated stores, about 70 stores)
segments.commentary: Same-store sales growth is negative per management; three older stores closed. Management described the model as manual retail with about 80% customised orders, typically Rs 40 lakh to Rs 1 crore per order. Large-format superlative living store of 72,000 sq ft and a Hyderabad flagship (opened about two months before the call) are the newer formats.

segments.name: B2B / builder mock-ups
segments.commentary: Builders are enquiring about branded furniture for show flats. Management said B2B gross margin is lower than B2C retail, but did not quantify the gap. Management said the company has not disclosed the B2B vs retail split.

guidance_outlook: Management says the existing manufacturing capacity (base about Rs 419-420 crore) can reach Rs 800+ crore revenue without new capacity, subject to product mix.
Management expects revenue to return to double-digit growth after the restructuring and store rationalisation is about 70% complete.
Management said it is too early to give H2 EBITDA margin guidance.

Management targets around 20% EBITDA margin for mature large-format stores after rentals, with 2-3 quarters to breakeven and fixed costs of about 10-11% of sales at maturity (initially 15-16%, falling to about 12%).
Management expects a possible reversal in Q3 of the Rs 2.83 crore exceptional charge tied to the former company secretary's alleged fraud, with recovery in process.
capex_capacity: Existing manufacturing capacity can support about Rs 800+ crore of revenue against a base of about Rs 419-420 crore, per management.
Hyderabad store is a pilot large-format store opened about two months before the call; the company plans to open more large-format stores in the four metros.
Management said it will shut smaller Stanley stores in key markets such as Delhi and consolidate into complete home solution stores.
Proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries into Stanley Lifestyles Ltd is in progress to simplify the corporate structure.
Management did not give a count of new store openings in FY27.
demand_pricing: Management said conversion cycles remain extended because customers wait for possession of new premium and luxury homes; recovery is slower than expected.
Management expects the drag from delayed handovers to ease from Q3 or early Q4 FY27.
Rupee depreciation pressured gross margin in Q2 FY27 (no gross margin figure was disclosed).

Management said the QCO on imported furniture may push individual buyers toward domestic products, though no timeline or sizing was given beyond an estimated USD 100 million of imported recliners and similar furniture.
Builder mock-up enquiries are rising; management said builders are increasingly showing branded furniture in show flats.

qa_highlights.question: Are delayed residential handovers a deferral of demand or orders already booked, and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book has improved but invoicing is slower as projects are handed over late; the effect should fade from Q3 or early Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue capability on current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current capacity can reach about Rs 800+ crore from a base of about Rs 419-420 crore, depending on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise faster than revenue, and what will drive H2 EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited increments, reversal of NPD cost capitalisation and senior management hiring; management said it is too early to guide H2 profitability.

qa_highlights.question: What is the same-store sales trend for stores older than three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said same-store sales growth is negative; detailed historical data for the 35 older stores would be shared by email.

qa_highlights.question: How does the superlative living store's profitability compare with the 20% EBITDA margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a mature store should reach about 20% EBITDA margin after rentals, though it acknowledged that rentals and other fixed costs reduce the margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for a share buyback given the low share price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would consider and explore a buyback, noting about Rs 170 crore of cash and promoter holding below the 75% limit.

risks_watch: Revenue remains below prior year on a half-yearly basis (H1 down about 3.6%), and same-store sales are negative.
Margin pressure from rupee depreciation and higher employee costs; EBITDA margin for H2 is not guided.
Dependence on residential handover timelines for premium and luxury housing demand.
Execution risk in large-format store rollout (Hyderabad pilot and the superlative living store) and in closing older stores.
Governance and control matters: former company secretary arrested over an alleged financial fraud; Rs 2.83 crore exceptional charge may reverse in Q3 FY27.
Pending amalgamation of subsidiaries and senior management changes.
summary.management_tone: Management was cautious on demand, saying the retail recovery is taking longer than expected, and it was non-committal on H2 profitability. It was more confident on the medium-term outlook, citing a Rs 800+ crore capacity headroom and the expected return to double-digit growth. Answers to shareholder questions on store-level economics and same-store sales were evasive, with data deferred to email.
key_quotes: The retail business is still operating in a challenging environment.
Customers are taking longer to finalize their purchases as they wait for possession of their homes.
While the sequential improvement is encouraging, our focus remains on improving profitability as newer stores mature.

rows.why: Three older stores already closed and smaller stores in Delhi and other key markets to be shut, with restructuring about 70% complete, though no count was given.
